race.name: Gravel Desert

climate.description: 2027 is the race's first March date. The organizer warns of strong winds depending on the day and dusty sectors on the long, open straights.

terrain.primary: Monegros hardpack gravel and farm tracks
terrain.surface: The organizer describes hardpack gravel with long straight sections that demand constant pedalling, loose corners and dusty sectors. It recommends 40-45 mm fast-rolling tires and a wide-range 1x or 2x setup for the Santa Quiteria climb. No paved/unpaved split is published.
features: Four feed zones and three water points
Assistance areas at Robres and Sariñena

gravel_god_rating.score_note: Gravel Desert sits at the top of Tier 3 on a fast 167 km desert course, a real pro race up front and Klassmark's race-day detail. It stays below Tier 2 because 1,500 m of climbing is modest, no field size has ever been published, and since 2024 it has changed month, start town and organizer.

biased_opinion.summary: On paper Gravel Desert is fast: 167 km, 1,500 m of gain, hardpack that rewards constant pedalling. The line to read twice is the organizer's own warning about strong winds, depending on the day, across open Monegros plains. It began as a small 2024 'edición cero' from Huesca, ran in Grañén as Gravel Desert by The Traka in April 2026, and returns on March 13, 2027 as round 2 of The Traka World Series. The pro race is real. The track record is short and keeps moving.
strengths: Round 2 of The Traka World Series
Published feed zones, water points and assistance areas
Fast hardpack that rewards steady power
About an hour from Zaragoza airport
weaknesses: Month, start town and organizer have changed since 2024
2027 prices and field size not published
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Go for an early-season pro race on fast desert gravel, and treat the wind as part of the course. Fitness gets you to Sariñena; a group gets you home.

final_verdict.one_liner: 167 km of Monegros hardpack where the wind sets the difficulty.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want an early-season Spanish race with a pro field, fast gravel and intermediate cutoffs that leave room for most riders. Wait if you need a published price or a race that has settled on a date.
final_verdict.alternatives: For the full Traka experience, race The Traka in Girona. For another Traka World Series round on forest gravel, race The River in Bouillon.

logistics.airport: Zaragoza airport is about an hour's drive and Barcelona about three; Huesca and Tardienta stations have regional and AVE trains.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Grañén is small: the organizer lists one hotel in town, plus options in Huesca (25 minutes), Tardienta, Sariñena and Frula. Book early.
logistics.food: On the 167 km, feed zones sit at km 22.2, 57.3, 85.2 and 131.2, with water at km 68.3, 124.4 and 145.6 and a feed at the finish.
logistics.packet_pickup: Grañén Sports Hall, Friday March 12 from 18:00 to 20:00 and race morning from 7:15 to 8:15.
logistics.parking: The organizer links van and motorhome parking; details not published.

history.founder: Asociación Espacio 108; organized by Klassmark since 2026
history.origin_story: Gravel Desert began as an 'edición cero' from Huesca on October 19, 2024, run by Asociación Espacio 108 with a 200 km route past Santa Quiteria and Sariñena. The first full edition ran from Grañén on September 13, 2025, won by Esmée Peperkamp and Tim Wollenberg. In 2026 it ran from Grañén on April 11 as Gravel Desert by The Traka, and for 2027 it moves to March 13.
notable_moments: 2024: 'edición cero' from Huesca, 200 km with 2,153 m of gain, run by Asociación Espacio 108
2025: first full edition on September 13 from Grañén; Tim Wollenberg won the sprint, Esmée Peperkamp the women's race
2026: April 11 in Grañén as Gravel Desert by The Traka, a Gravel Earth Series round; Geerike Schreurs and Mads Würtz Schmidt both won solo
2027: round 2 of The Traka World Series, March 13
history.reputation: A young, fast Monegros race with Klassmark production and a calendar slot that keeps moving.

course_description.character: The 2027 167 km track starts and finishes in Grañén with 1,500 m of gain. It links Tardienta, Robres, Alcubierre, Lanaja, Albalatillo, Sariñena and San Lorenzo del Flumen on hardpack farm tracks, long straights and dusty corners, with Santa Quiteria as the climb to gear for.

migration_notes: 2026-11-05: Added as a new profile after The Traka World Series named Gravel Desert round 2 for 2027. Organizer publishes March 13, 2027 with 167 km / 1,500 m and 85 km / 900 m tracks; prices and field cap are not published. The program lists an 18:00 finish cutoff for the 167 km and the track page 19:50; vitals carry both until the organizer settles it. History links the 2024 Espacio 108 'edición cero' to the Klassmark race through the shared name, the graveldesert.com site and route towns (Santa Quiteria, Sariñena). The 2025 Gravel Earth Series calendar listed the round as 'Monegros Desert Festival' on July 26; no 2025 result was verified. Cyclingnews' 2026 report was readable only to its headline, so 2026 podium places below the winners are not recorded.

2026-11-06: Sport Aragón reports the first full edition ran from Grañén on September 13, 2025 (157 km; Esmée Peperkamp, Tim Wollenberg); the 2024 Huesca ride stays as the 'edición cero'. Editions table now lists 2024, 2025 and 2026.

logistics.explanation: Moderate planning. Zaragoza airport is about an hour away and Barcelona about three [6]; race weekend is compact, with bib pickup, start and finish all at Grañén Sports Hall [4].

length.explanation: Long, not ultra. The 167 km track is about 103.8 miles [2], with an 85 km option below it [3].

technicality.explanation: Fast more than technical. The organizer describes hardpack, long straights, loose corners and dusty sectors, and recommends 40-45 mm fast-rolling tires [2].

elevation.explanation: Moderate. 1,500 m (4,921 ft) over 167 km [2] is under 10 m of climbing per kilometre; the organizer singles out Santa Quiteria as the climb to gear for [2].

climate.explanation: Wind is the variable. 2027 is the first March date after an April edition in 2026 [1][10], and the organizer warns of strong winds depending on the day and dusty sectors [2].

altitude.explanation: Irrelevant. Grañén sits low on the Monegros plain [14]; the organizer does not publish a high point.

adventure.explanation: Memorable for Europe. The route crosses desert landscape the organizer sells as wind-shaped [1], linking farm towns from Tardienta and Robres to Lanaja and Sariñena [2]: open horizons, not wilderness.

prestige.explanation: Young, with serious backing. It ran as a Gravel Earth Series round in 2026 [11] and is round 2 of The Traka World Series in 2027 [7][8], but its history only goes back to a 2024 'edición cero' [12].

race_quality.explanation: Professional on paper. The 167 km publishes four feed zones, three water points, two assistance areas and a cutoff at every stop [2], with live tracking [1]. One loose end: the program says the finish closes at 18:00 [4], the track page 19:50 [2].

experience.explanation: Enjoyable, not yet mythic. A Friday rider presentation and a single-hall start and finish in Grañén [4] make a tidy weekend, but the race hasn't held one date long enough to build a legend [12][10][1].

community.explanation: Unproven. No field size has been published for any edition, and since its 2024 start from Huesca [12] the race has changed start town, month and organizer [1][5].

field_depth.explanation: Strong pro racing. Geerike Schreurs and Mads Würtz Schmidt both won solo in 2026 [9], and the 2027 PRO category races for cash prizes [5] in a series that pays EUR 8,000 per round [8].

value.explanation: Fair, pending a price. 2027 fees are not out yet [1], against seven support points on the 167 km course [2].

expenses.explanation: Moderate. Fees are not out yet [1]; the real cost is getting to Aragón and a room in a small town or in Huesca, 25 minutes away [6].
